tagline: BCM Input Brief · AI process-leadership perspective

facts.v: N2 (2nm, GAA) volume production 2025 Q4; A16 2H 2026

context: TSMC is the world's largest and most process-advanced pure-play wafer foundry: it only manufactures — it does not design or sell branded chips, and its "we don't compete with our customers" stance is the foundation of its trust. In 2025, AI/HPC overtook smartphones to become its largest platform. The following is not a generic company profile but is organized by note 1's BCM input fields: business objectives at the top row, with the capability inventory and metadata as the body.

objectives.name: Process-generation leadership
objectives.kpi: Leading-node volume-production timeline (N2 in production, A16 2H26); PPA lead at equal power

objectives.name: AI / HPC revenue growth
objectives.kpi: HPC revenue share (58% in 2025); AI accelerators 2024–29 CAGR mid-to-high 50%

objectives.name: Global capacity resilience
objectives.kpi: Overseas-fab yield and profitability (Arizona first-year profit US$514M)

objectives.name: Profitability and capital efficiency
objectives.kpi: Gross margin (59.9% in 2025); capex efficiency (2026 capex US$52–56B)

capabilities.name: Process technology R&D
capabilities.definition: Develop new nodes and transistor architectures (GAA nanosheet, backside power delivery Super Power Rail)

capabilities.name: Yield management and process integration
capabilities.definition: Drive up yield, converge defects, feed metrology and inspection back into the process

capabilities.name: Advanced packaging
capabilities.definition: Integrate chiplets and HBM via CoWoS / SoIC / InFO 2.5D/3D packaging

capabilities.name: Customer design enablement
capabilities.definition: Run the OIP ecosystem, provide PDK / IP / EDA certification to shorten customer ramp-up

capabilities.name: Capacity planning and allocation
capabilities.definition: Decide capacity investment, allocate capacity to customers

capabilities.name: Global manufacturing footprint
capabilities.definition: Build and operate overseas fabs (Arizona / Japan / Germany)

capabilities.name: Supply chain management
capabilities.definition: Coordinate supply of equipment, materials, specialty gases, and HBM

capabilities.name: Facilities and equipment engineering
capabilities.definition: Operate and maintain cleanrooms, facility systems, and equipment

capabilities.name: Quality and reliability
capabilities.definition: Validate reliability, run the quality management system

capabilities.name: Capital expenditure and financial management
capabilities.definition: Plan capex, manage depreciation and finance

capabilities.name: IP and information security
capabilities.definition: Protect process secrets and IP, defend information security

capabilities.name: Compliance and export control
capabilities.definition: Respond to export controls and tariffs, enforce regulatory compliance

capabilities.name: Talent management
capabilities.definition: Recruit, train, and retain talent (including overseas assignments)

capabilities.name: Sustainability ESG
capabilities.definition: Manage energy, water, net-zero, and environmental governance

notes: The objectives' attainment values (58%, 59.9%, US$514M, etc.) come from public financial reports; each capability's "industry-typical KPI" is only a generic metric name, not a TSMC internal target value (note 1, L106).
Pace layer is a strategic judgment "relative to a given objective"; here it takes the "push AI process leadership" perspective. Change the objective and the colours change (note 1, L124).
Internal metadata (owner / supporting systems / data in-out / data readiness 1–5) is not public — all fields TBD (note 1, L256–262).
Disputed figures such as the largest customer (NVIDIA vs Apple) and the 2025 revenue basis are covered in the data notes of the company-context brief.
